request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Patient Age: 45 years
Gender: Male
Date of admission: [REDACTED]
Date of discharge: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with symptoms of intermittent fever, chills and rigors along with night sweats, loss of appetite, and weight loss. The patient also had a transient macular rash and generalized painful lymphadenopathy. Synovitis involving lower limb small joints was noted following the presentation that progressed to larger joints in the lower and upper limbs. Laboratory investigations revealed high white cell counts, normocytic anemia and high inflammatory markers which were in a rising trend following the onset of arthritis. The patient was diagnosed as a case of DLBCL following a lymph node biopsy.

Treatment:
The patient was started on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents and colchicine for the arthritis but there was no response to treatment. Treatment with RCHOP chemotherapy commenced which showed a marked response in the synovitis following the first cycle of therapy. The patient completed the chemotherapy with intermittent infections.

Summary:
The patient presented with symptoms of intermittent fever, chills, and rigors along with night sweats, loss of appetite, and weight loss. The patient had synovitis involving the small and large joints of the upper and lower limbs with a lower limb predominance. Laboratory investigations revealed high white cell counts and anemia. A lymph node biopsy was positive for DLBCL. The patient underwent RCHOP chemotherapy which resulted in the complete resolution of synovitis. The patient was discharged in stable condition with a follow-up plan for further evaluation and management.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: C83**

The episode is best classified as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), which was established by lymph node biopsy and treated with R-CHOP. The fever, sweats, weight loss, and synovitis were manifestations of the lymphoma, and the RCHOP treatment resolved the synovitis. DLBCL falls under category C83, Non-follicular lymphoma, in the malignant neoplasms chapter (C).
